topics.title: The AI wage premium hit 56% — and it's the postings that don't mention AI that are vanishing
topics.why: Fresh PwC/Indeed data this month puts a hard number on the two-speed jobs market: a 56% wage premium for AI-skilled roles even as overall vacancies fall about 10%.

topics.title: 84% of companies still haven't redesigned a single job around AI
topics.why: New 2026 workforce research shows AI tool access reaching 60% of workers while most firms just bolt AI onto old workflows instead of restructuring roles — explains why so many rollouts feel underwhelming.

topics.title: Inside the 9% of companies actually winning at AI
topics.why: New enterprise research isolates a small 'Pacesetter' cohort getting measurable AI ROI with a repeatable playbook, worth breaking down for readers building leverage inside their own companies.

topics.title: The AI trainer economy just crossed $12B — and the money moved to domain experts
topics.why: Spend on human feedback and training data is on pace to nearly double by 2027, with pay shifting sharply from generalist labeling toward $80+/hr specialist evaluation work.

topics.title: What Reddit actually says about AI training-gig platforms before you sign up
topics.why: A wave of new Mindrift/Mercor/Outlier-style platforms this year has produced real community skepticism about pay claims and application funnels, worth separating from the marketing copy.
